abstract: Mitochondrial trifunctional protein deficiency (TFP-D) is a rare, life threatening long-chain fatty acid oxidation disorder caused by variants in either the HADHA or HADHB subunits, leading to toxic metabolite accumulation and systemic energy deficiency. Current dietary management strategies are only partially effective and fail to prevent long term morbidity and mortality. Here, we developed a lipid nanoparticle (LNP) mediated mRNA replacement strategy to restore TFP function in a moderate severity TFP-D mouse model by delivering both Hadha and Hadhb mRNA. In cultured TFP-D mouse fibroblasts, dual mRNA delivery, but not single subunit replacement, rescued long-chain fatty acid oxidation and revealed a dominant negative effect exerted by the endogenous M404K variant Hadhb. In vivo, intravenous administration of dual mRNA-LNPs restored hepatic TFP expression, reduced circulating long-chain acylcarnitines, and improved physiological performance in aged TFP-D mice. Notably, intravenous delivery of dual mRNA LNPs significantly rescued cold tolerance test (CTT) performance by up to 71.6% compared to untreated and healthy controls. Together, these findings establish dual subunit LNP-mRNA delivery as a promising therapeutic strategy for TFP-D and support its potential applicability to other long-chain fatty acid oxidation disorders.
